name: Financial Aid in Plain Language
title: Financial Aid in Plain Language
answer: Financial aid in plain language means using AI to help draft clear guides to the FAFSA and to explain common problems, while keeping official details tied to Federal Student Aid at studentaid.gov. It matters because the form confuses many families, and students who do not complete it often miss aid they qualify for. The text says personalized help connected to a student's real FAFSA status can improve completion and college enrollment, while generic national campaigns did not work.

sections.body: The FAFSA presents a significant obstacle for many families. It asks for tax information and includes steps that confuse even parents with strong educational backgrounds. When students do not complete it, they often miss out on aid they qualify for. Plain language help can make a difference. The idea is to use AI to draft plain language guides and explain common problems, so families can understand the process and take the next step.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text does not give grade bands for this idea. It describes a counseling, college, and career setting where counselors can use AI to draft plain language guides to the FAFSA and to explain common problems. Financial aid nights are a good place to combine these supports. A school can offer guides in families' languages, explain the steps, and have staff available to help families fill out the form. The text also points to Chapter 14 on translating materials with human review, and it says financial aid information is too important to leave to an unchecked translation.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text cites a multidistrict trial (Page et al., 2020) finding that personalized text messages based on each student's FAFSA status improved completion and college enrollment. The messages told students exactly where they stood and what to do next. It also cites national campaigns without that personal connection that did not work (Bird et al., 2021). The text says the connection to real data and a real school made the difference. The text does not give a separate evidence label beyond these citations.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets limits on how AI should be used here. Official information from Federal Student Aid at studentaid.gov should be the source for all details, since rules change. Families should never enter tax or identity information into a general chat tool. A counselor or trained volunteer should help families with the form itself, so the decisions about the form and the family's information stay with people rather than the AI. Translation should include human review, because financial aid information is too important to leave to an unchecked translation.
